sources.entry: snowshare - File and link sharing platform with URL shortening, code snippet sharing, and file uploads, featuring customizable expiration, privacy settings, and QR codes. (Demo) CC0-1.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: SnowShare is a self-hosted web app for sharing files, short links and text/code pastes, with optional expiration, view limits, passwords and QR codes.
summary.what_it_does: Handles three kinds of shares: file uploads (resumable via tus, multiple files per share, browser previews for common formats), a URL shortener with optional custom slugs, and text or code pastes with syntax highlighting. Any share can have an expiration date, a maximum view count, a password and a QR code. The admin side provides user accounts (email/password or OAuth), optional email verification and CAPTCHA, separate quotas for anonymous and logged-in users, custom branding, and local disk or S3-compatible storage. A REST API under /api/v1 uses API keys, with OpenAPI docs served per instance. The interface is translated into English, French, Spanish, German, Dutch and Polish.
use_cases: share large files with resumable uploads
share code snippets or text pastes
temporary links with expiry and password
how_to_run: Create a folder with docker-compose.yml defining a postgres:16-alpine db service and the turodev/snowshare:latest app service
Generate a .env file with POSTGRES_PASSWORD, NEXTAUTH_URL and NEXTAUTH_SECRET (openssl rand -base64 32)
Development: git clone the repo, npm install, cp .env.example .env, npx prisma migrate dev, npm run dev
notable: Resumable uploads via tus, so interrupted transfers can continue
Admin panel changes quotas, OAuth, SMTP, CAPTCHA, branding and S3 without restart
Works with S3-compatible storage such as MinIO, Garage or R2
Reverse proxy guidance covering X-Forwarded-For and TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT
Docker image built for amd64 and arm64
caveats: Requires PostgreSQL and a Docker or Node.js 24+ setup; four variables must be set before it runs
Large uploads can fail behind a reverse proxy unless the request body size limit is raised (e.g. client_max_body_size 0; on nginx)
Telemetry is on by default, sending anonymous stats to Plausible unless TELEMETRY=false is set
